To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding mode and affinity of trinitrophenol derivatives of ATP and ADP are distinct from the parent compounds, and the crystal structures explain the origin of “fluorescence superactivation.”
the trinitro group binds in place of the adenine ring in the nucleotide-binding pocket of Ca2+- ATPase, and the side chain of Arg-684 is critical for binding of trinitrophenol to the E1P state.

the trinitro group in trinitrophenol-ATP, trinitro-ADP, and trinitro-AMP binds to the adenine binding pocket of the nucleotide binding site of Ca2+- ATPase in the absence and presence of Ca2+ and that the binding mode is different from that of the parent nucleotides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the energy transducing P-type ATPase family.
elucidating the structural and mechanistic bases of the function of P-type ATPases.
the structural basis for the function of Ca2+-pumping ATPases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of the trinitropbenzene group to the adenine binding site is the primary determinant of the fluorescence properties of the trinitronphenyl derivatives.
ATP and its analogs are very flexible molecules and can be accommodated in different binding sites by different protein structures.

the trinitrobenzene moiety of the trinitrophenoxy group of trinitrophenylation reagents can bind in different orientations to the same binding site, depending on the conformation of the protein and the presence or absence of a metal ion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP and ADP are highly adaptable to different binding sites.
ATP and its trinitrophenol derivatives have distinct and different binding modes in the nucleotide-binding site of the P-type ATPase.
trinitrophenylation of ATP and ADP is a very effective strategy to stabilize the nucleotide binding to Ca2+- and Na+,K+-ATPases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trinitro group can be used as a probe to monitor the nucleotide-binding pocket of P-type ATPase and to study the structural dynamics of the nucleotide-binding site in the E2 states.
